review_notes: I read the whole target file and the wedge lemmas it uses in TransmissionWedge.lean and VertexWedgeRankFormula.lean. The wedgeAddDivisor_add, _sub, _zsmul and _one_chip_* lemmas carry no @[simp] attribute. Only the presentation iff lemmas in the *Presentation.lean files are simp. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about what simp does. The rest of the file (the profile defs and the iff theorems) has no simp problem I could justify. I deliberately did not suggest making the add/sub/zsmul lemmas simp: it would change simp normal forms elsewhere, and I did not check that. The finding is a modest one, about a missing reusable lemma for the chip-lift rewrite.

rw [← wedgeAddDivisor_one_chip_left G H x y p,
      wedgeAddDivisor_zsmul]
    simp
findings.problem: Each of the three twist theorems (this file's sameLeft and sameRight, plus `wedgeAddDivisor_transmissionTwist` in TransmissionWedge.lean) re-proves the same local fact by hand. The fact is that `n • oneChip (inl u)` or `n • oneChip (wedgeRightVertex ..)` equals `wedgeAddDivisor (n • oneChip u) 0` or `wedgeAddDivisor 0 (n • oneChip v)`. Each proof rewrites `← wedgeAddDivisor_one_chip_*`, applies `wedgeAddDivisor_zsmul`, then calls `simp` to clear `n • 0`. There are six copies of this block. The interface has no lemma for a scalar multiple of a lifted chip. The only chip lemmas run from `wedgeAddDivisor ... = oneChip ...`, so any use on `n • oneChip (inl u)` needs a manual reverse rewrite and a cleanup `simp`. The final `rw [hP, hQ, wedgeAddDivisor_add, wedgeAddDivisor_sub]; simp` is also hand-sequenced. The additive combination lemmas are not part of any simp set.
findings.proposed_change: In TransmissionWedge.lean, next to `wedgeAddDivisor_one_chip_left` and `_right`, add `wedgeAddDivisor_zsmul_one_chip_left` and `_right`. They would state `wedgeAddDivisor G H x y (n • oneChip u) 0 = n • oneChip (G := vertexWedge G H x y) (Sum.inl u)` and `wedgeAddDivisor G H x y 0 (n • oneChip v) = n • oneChip (G := vertexWedge G H x y) (wedgeRightVertex G H x y v)`. The direction goes from the wedge-lift form to the plain-chip form, matching the existing chip lemmas. Optionally mark them @[simp], since the right-hand side is smaller. Then hP and hQ become one-line `.symm` uses, and the three twist theorems shrink to the same four-step `rw`/`simp`. Better still, derive sameLeft and sameRight from one shared lemma instead of three copies.
findings.benefit: The chip-lift rewriting lives in one named, reusable lemma with a fixed orientation instead of six copied proof blocks. A change in how wedge divisors or chips are represented then needs one fix. Downstream proofs about transmission twists on wedges can use the lemma, or `simp` if it is tagged, without repeating the reverse-rewrite-plus-cleanup pattern.

wedgeAddDivisor G H x y (oneChip u) 0 =

rw [← wedgeAddDivisor_one_chip_right G H x y p,
